items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public service law, in relation to directing the public service commission to conduct an in-depth public interest analysis of proposed mergers by telephone corporations and other telecommunications services providers over which said commission has jurisdiction
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S7263

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the public service law, in relation to directing the
public service commission to conduct an in-depth public interest
analysis of proposed mergers by telephone corporations and other
telecommunications services providers over which said commission has
jurisdiction


 PURPOSE :
This bill would require the public service commission to conduct a
closer scrutiny of proposed telecommunications industry mergers and/or
transfers of control, and to enumerate the public interest factors
analyzed during such scrutiny. The bill declares that except where the
public interest requires a contrary result, a portion of the benefits
of such mergers should be returned to the state's rate payers directly
or by reinvestment in instate infrastructure.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
This law would amend section 99 and section 100 of the public service
law.

 JUSTIFICATION :
The public interest requires that the Public Service Commission's
(Commission) analysis of mergers and conclusions drawn there from
arise from objective and verifiable empirical evidence, rather than
from unsupported statements of policy or conclusory observations.
Further, the public interest requires that the Commission's analysis
be enumerated for public scrutiny in a transparent manner.

As other states such as New Jersey and California have previously
legislated, it is additionally in the public interest to require a
portion of the benefits of telecommunications mergers to be returned
to the state's ratepayer's as refunds, reinvestment in the
infrastructure providing E-911 services or other services, or to
finance repairs, maintenance or new construction that might otherwise
be unfunded. As noted in the Assembly Committee on Corporations,
Authorities and Commission's Interim Report on Telephone Service
Quality, and in numerous service quality proceedings at the
Commission, additional investment in telecommunications company
physical plant is vital to better service, and public safety.

Consequently, this legislation requires the Public Service Commission
to conduct its analysis upon an enumerated list of public interest
factors, which increases the participation of the p\wlic and other
stakeholder groups in such proceedings and enhances the transparency
and accountability of the merger analysis process.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
S.7263 (2007) - Energy and Telecommunications
A.10043 (2007) - Passed Assembly
S.6686 (2006) - Energy and Telecommunications
A.9809 (2006) - Rules

 FISCAL IMPACT ON THE STATE :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the 120th day after it shall have become
law, and any rule or regulation necessary for the timely
implementation of this act on its effective date shall be promulgated
within 90 days of such date.
